title: The Brunies boys join the band
summary: Laine's band was all young boys; the Brunies brothers joined at about eight to ten, and their violinist father trained them and played on corners.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. Yeah. Now, did you have anybody else in that band who was older than you were? Were there boys who were older than you were? No. No. They were all your age or younger? Yeah, they were. Yeah. Fifteen and sixteen-year-old kids. That's the song.

All children. Now, when William Brunish started to play with me, when I took him to play with Alto, he was eight years old. Is that right? My boy was only eight years old. And Abby Brunish was about a year or two older then. Then Richie was about the same thing, two years or two older. See?

I took them all in the band. And I'll tell you about the Brunish boys. The daddy was a good musicianer, good violin player, mighty good violin player. And he loved music. He sure loved music. That old man sure loved music. So he'd get them kids all together, he's kids, buy them old instruments and stuff, and practice. And get out on the street with them kids. Is that right? On the street and play at the corners. If you give them nickels, all right, if you didn't, it was all right too. That was old man, brother.
